mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate compresses equity valuations by increasing the discount rate for future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is rising, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 104.5), the manufacturing sector slowdown signals reduced corporate capacity utilization and lower near-term earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 104.5, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS is rising, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 6.0%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 6.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%) signals a dual stress on the labor market and monetary policy, which together depress corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of UNRATE rising and FEDFUNDS > 3.0% fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong economic growth (GDPC1 QoQ > 1.0%), the S&P 500 tends to experience positive returns over the next 60 days due to elevated corporate earnings growth and investor optimism.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances when GDPC1 QoQ > 1.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.02.
